Playbook.name: Windows — LSASS Memory Dump via Known Credential-Theft Tooling - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A command line indicating an LSASS memory dump ran - procdump on lsass, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or a tool referencing lsass with dump semantics. Triage question: is this credential theft from LSASS, or a legitimate diagnostic dump?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Dumping LSASS yields plaintext/NTLM credentials and Kerberos tickets for logged-on users - a primary credential-theft technique.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: LSASS dump
Signal.Details: cmdline referencing lsass with procdump/comsvcs MiniDump/rundll32 dump semantics.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the LSASS dump is credential theft or a legitimate diagnostic.

Step.name: Confirm the LSASS dump command
Step.Purpose: The command shows the dumping method (procdump/comsvcs/taskmgr) and target.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE cl LIKE "*lsass*" AND (cl LIKE "*procdump*" OR cl LIKE "*comsvcs*minidump*" OR cl LIKE "*-ma*" OR cl LIKE "*dump*" OR cl LIKE "*rundll32*minidump*") | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, user.name, process.command_line | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: rundll32 comsvcs.dll MiniDump <lsass pid> is a hallmark of hands-on credential theft. procdump -ma lsass by a non-admin is malicious. A Microsoft-support diagnostic under a ticket is the benign exception.

Step.name: Did the dumping account then move laterally / use credentials
Step.Purpose: LSASS dump followed by new logons/lateral movement indicates the stolen credentials are being used.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4624","4648","5145") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType) BY src | SORT c DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: 4648 (explicit credential logon) or new network logons/pipe access from the host after the dump suggests harvested credentials are being reused - escalate.

Node.Condition: An LSASS dump via procdump/comsvcs by a non-admin/normal account, especially with follow-on credential use.
Node.Result: True Positive (Credential Theft - IR, reset exposed credentials)

Node.Condition: A Microsoft-support/diagnostic LSASS dump by an admin under a documented ticket.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-LSASS-CMD, INV-02-LSASS-FOLLOWON to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the diagnostic; close as false_positive.
Isolate the host; open IR; reset ALL credentials that were logged on to the host (incl. privileged).
Hunt the dumping tool's origin and other hosts.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An EDR/AV product legitimately reading LSASS.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
